feedback.answered: Six implementation responsibilities are confirmed in scope by executed clean-copy checks and correspondence reviews, each described by the accepted claim it answers: the follower's cached last-log identity is not updated on the two appendEntries error returns, so a faithful to the interface store failure or an undecodable deprecated peer entry leaves the node rejecting an otherwise valid AppendEntries for the truncated range (two independent scenarios, executions e4bd66d3 and ccb85562); the leader answers inflight futures with ErrAbortedByRestore before the fallible snapshot creation, so a failed restore leaves a definite 'write effectively failed' signal on operations whose entries remain logged (execution 75816d44); the monotonic-store snapshot install empties the log store without re-deriving the cached identity, so a follower whose cached index exceeds the installed snapshot index rejects the leader's post-install AppendEntries (execution 080acf9a); FileSnapshotStore.List does not meet the SnapshotStore contract for an inversely ordered retained pair, and both named consumers inherit it - the leader ships the lower-index snapshot (execution c3121fc5) and startup recovery adopts it (execution 0182ff14, confirmed as its own recovery duty); and a bootstrap whose log write fails after the term write leaves the store looking already bootstrapped so the ordinary retry is rejected (execution e71729d1). Each rests on a constructed premise of the same shape - a faithfully failing or monotonic store, an undecodable payload, or an inversely ordered retention - and the correspondence reviews state which of those premises production reachability leaves open.
remaining: Whether production stores, leaders or histories reach each confirmed failure position, and whether any confirmed defect also carries a safety consequence rather than the bounded availability or contract consequence confirmed.
Two deferred surfaces are recorded for follow-up: the Raft.Restore error-reporting ambiguity and the Apply/ApplyLog future that can be abandoned at shutdown when BatchApplyCh buffers the channel.

The FSM batch manager details, the tcp transport stream layer and connection pool, the TimeoutNow-without-term residual, and the part of startup reconstruction still sourced only from the store interfaces remain unread or partially read.
The pre-existing unknown that the term-first comparator may be the intended ordering, in which case the interface wording is the incorrect statement, remains open for the ordering findings.
